title: Rigidity of local morphisms to an ordinary affine monoid spectrum
statement: Let P be a fine commutative monoid and T any space with a sheaf of commutative monoids, with unsharpened affine spectrum A(P), canonical numerator sections and local morphisms as in [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup] and [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization]. If local morphisms f,g : T -> A(P) have equal pullbacks of all canonical global numerator sections, then f=g as sheafed-space morphisms. This is a uniqueness assertion only and asserts no existence of a morphism for arbitrary section data.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 3.1.8(i) and its proof, printed p.99, using 3.1.2--3.1.6, pp.98--99. This is the unsharpened assertion (i), not the sharp-stalk assertion (ii). No Stacks tag states this monoidal-space result.

proof.text: For a prime q, take its smallest neighborhood D(b) from [lem-trf-monoid-prime-minimal-neighborhood]. Every germ of the ordinary structure sheaf is uniquely its section on that smallest neighborhood, with sections P_b=P-(P\q); in the local-fraction construction and its sheafification this is the usual localization stalk. The same lemma implies that the canonical germ of p is a unit exactly when p is outside q. Pullback commutes with germs. By locality, at each t the membership p in f(t) and p in g(t) is therefore equivalent to the common pulled-back section having nonunit germ at t. Extensionality of prime ideals and of continuous maps gives equality of the underlying base maps.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 3.1.8(i) and its proof, printed p.99, using 3.1.2--3.1.6, pp.98--99. This is the unsharpened assertion (i), not the sharp-stalk assertion (ii). No Stacks tag states this monoidal-space result.

proof.text: After identifying the base maps, on D(a) naturality forces the image of a numerator p to be the restriction of its global pullback, and preservation of units forces the image of a inverse to be the unique inverse of the pulled-back a. Every element of P[a inverse] is p/a^n, so the two section homomorphisms agree on D(a). Clause (a) of [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-morphism-on-basis], applied with target the pushforward of the sheaf on T, extends equality from this principal-open basis to all opens. Consequently the sheaf maps and the sheafed-space morphisms agree. No existence theorem or affine Hom bijection has been used.

mathlib_searches.query: Two local morphisms of monoidal spaces into an ordinary affine monoid spectrum are equal when they pull back each canonical numerator to the same global section.
A local morphism into the unsharpened spectrum of a fine commutative monoid is determined by its homomorphism on canonical global numerator sections.
